answer: An agent economy can put every newcomer on a narrow admission ledge: only a limited number of identity slots open each epoch, each requiring a locked deposit of scarce working capital. Peers then verify the claimant by a live signed puzzle bound to that slot's nonce, so a batch of sockpuppets cannot reuse one proof. The old fable that cheap copies can vote as many times as they like fails here, because each fake ID must buy its own slot and wait out the lock; as slots fill, the market price of remaining deposits climbs in a spiral, so the attacker's cost per extra identity keeps rising.
